turns.content: For 1-bromobenzene-2-d with NaNH2 in liquid ammonia, place Br at C1, D at C2, and H at C6. Identify the benzyne elimination-addition mechanism and the two possible ortho eliminations.
Analyze the first of the two ortho-elimination pathways identified above. What benzyne label pattern and product result after amide addition and protonation?
Analyze the other ortho-elimination pathway. List the products of amide attack at either benzyne terminus followed by protonation, retaining any isotope label that remains after elimination.
Compare the labeled molecular graphs from both pathways, preserving D, and decide which products are equivalent or distinct.
Name each distinct organic product and determine the total count.
Check the count by following deuterium loss or retention and the symmetry of the two benzyne attack sites.
Report the distinct products and their number.
